counterexample.positions: [0, 100) with liquidity L and [100, 200) with liquidity L, so tick 100 has gross liquidity 2L and net liquidity 0
counterexample.explanation: The repair includes an aligned start tick only when its net liquidity is non-zero. Tick 100 is initialized but its net is 0, so it is skipped. The liquidity result happens to stay right (L at both ends), so this fails only if requirement 4 is read as 'every initialized tick the walk passes', as the reference repair and the functional suite read it. The hook then does not update tick 100's reward growth, so the reward earned above tick 100 by [100, 200) is credited to [0, 100).

summary: The repair sets currentTick to startTick + 1 only when the start tick is a multiple of the spacing and its net liquidity is non-zero. An initialized start tick whose net liquidity is zero is still skipped; every other case is handled correctly.
